kaps_punt: Kenmerke van die Maan - die Maan is 'n bal van rots in die ruimte; daar is geen lug en water op die Maan nie; die Maan is kleiner as die Aarde; die Maan is nader aan die Aarde as die Son

items.bewering: 'n Bal van rots sonder lug
items.blok: titel
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): a rocky body with 'a very thin and tenuous atmosphere called an exosphere. It is not breathable.' NASA lunar atmosphere page (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/lunar-atmosphere/): 'Yes, but just barely'. 'Sonder lug' is right in the everyday sense of breathable air; the exosphere is so thin that its molecules rarely meet.

items.bewering: Van die Aarde af sien ons die Son, die Maan en die sterre.
items.blok: Die Aarde se naaste groot buurman
items.bron: Anyone can see this; NASA APOD (https://apod.nasa.gov/rjn/apod/ap990818.html) describes the Sun and the Moon each appearing about half a degree across in our sky.

items.bewering: Die Maan is 'n groot bal van rots wat altyd in die ruimte om die Aarde beweeg.
items.blok: Die Aarde se naaste groot buurman
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): completes an orbit around Earth in about 27 days at an average distance of 384,400 km; surface of rock and rocky debris. Britannica (https://britannica.com/question/What-is-the-Moon): Earth's sole natural satellite.

items.bewering: Dit is nie 'n ster nie en ook nie 'n planeet nie.
items.blok: Die Aarde se naaste groot buurman
items.bron: Britannica, 'What is the Moon?' (https://britannica.com/question/What-is-the-Moon): Earth's sole natural satellite, so neither a star nor a planet.

items.bewering: Die Maan is die Aarde se naaste groot buurman in die ruimte.
items.blok: Die Aarde se naaste groot buurman
items.bron: Britannica (https://britannica.com/question/What-is-the-Moon) calls the Moon Earth's 'nearest large celestial body'. The word 'groot' is the qualifier that makes it true: artificial satellites and some small near-Earth asteroids pass closer. The 'buurman' picture (near, and next to us) holds.

items.bewering: Die Maan se oppervlak is 'n los laag fyn grys stof en gebreekte klip.
items.blok: Hoe die Maan se oppervlak lyk
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): 'a rubble pile of charcoal-gray, powdery dust, and rocky debris called the lunar regolith'. Brown University, 14 July 2026 (https://www.brown.edu/news/2026-07-14/moon-regolith): 'the layer of loose dust and rock that drapes the entire lunar surface'.

items.bewering: Op die meeste plekke is daardie laag dieper as wat 'n mens lank is.
items.blok: Hoe die Maan se oppervlak lyk
items.bron: Brown University, 14 July 2026 (https://www.brown.edu/news/2026-07-14/moon-regolith): the regolith averages about 6 m in the highlands and about 4 m in the maria. Older estimates are deeper still (10-15 m in the highlands; a review gives 1-8 m in the maria and up to 40 m in the highlands, see https://scholarspace.manoa.hawaii.edu/items/1b4bfc92-1614-43e1-96e6-1540f9da1539). The highlands cover most of the surface, so on every estimate found the layer is deeper than an adult is tall (about 1.7 m) 'op die meeste plekke'.

items.bewering: Onder die laag lê harde rots.
items.blok: Hoe die Maan se oppervlak lyk
items.bron: Brown University, 14 July 2026 (https://www.brown.edu/news/2026-07-14/moon-regolith): impacts that 'penetrate through the regolith layer to reach bedrock' throw up boulders, which is how the study measured the thickness. In the highlands the rock underneath is cracked, but rock lying under the loose layer is correct at this level.

items.bewering: Daar groei geen gras, geen bome en geen ander plante nie.
items.blok: Hoe die Maan se oppervlak lyk
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): no evidence of any living things of its own; the weak atmosphere and lack of liquid water 'cannot support life as we know it'.

items.bewering: Daar dryf ook nooit 'n wolk bo die Maan nie.
items.blok: Hoe die Maan se oppervlak lyk
items.bron: NASA Space Place (https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/craters/en): 'no wind, no weather'. NASA (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/lunar-atmosphere/): only an extremely thin exosphere, so no weather clouds can form. Caveat, not a contradiction: LADEE found a permanent, extremely thin, invisible 'dust cloud' 10-260 km above the Moon (CU Boulder/LASP, https://lasp.colorado.edu/2015/06/17/moon-engulfed-in-permanent-lopsided-dust-cloud/). That is not a 'wolk' in the Grade 4 sense of something you could see drifting overhead, so the sentence stands.

items.bewering: Die Maan se landskap is byna oral net klip en stof.
items.blok: Hoe die Maan se oppervlak lyk
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): regolith of dust and rocky debris. 'Byna' leaves room for the polar ice the lesson mentions later.

items.bewering: Oor die hele oppervlak van die Maan lê daar ronde merke. Hierdie merke is kraters, en elkeen is 'n holte met 'n rand rondom.
items.blok: Die ronde kraters
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): a steady rain of asteroids, meteoroids and comets 'strikes the surface of the Moon, leaving numerous craters behind'. NASA Earth Observatory (https://www.earthobservatory.nasa.gov/IOTD/view.php?id=39769): craters on the Moon are virtually permanent. Craters are found across the whole Moon, though there are fewer on the dark maria. A bowl with a raised rim is the standard crater shape (OpenStax Astronomy 9.3, https://openstax.org/books/astronomy/pages/9-3-impact-craters). Old craters have worn rims, but at this level 'elkeen' is acceptable.

items.bewering: Die meeste kraters is gemaak deur rotse wat uit die ruimte gekom het.
items.blok: Die ronde kraters
items.bron: NASA Space Place (https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/craters/en): craters come from space rocks hitting the surface. NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): asteroids, meteoroids and comets. OpenStax 9.3 (https://openstax.org/books/astronomy/pages/9-3-impact-craters): impact is the accepted explanation. 'Die meeste' correctly leaves room for the few volcanic craters, and 'rotse' is a fair Grade 4 word even though comets also contain ice.

items.bewering: So 'n rots tref die Maan en slaan 'n gat in die klip.
items.blok: Die ronde kraters
items.bron: NASA Space Place (https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/craters/en). Mapping checked: the picture is an impact that leaves a hole, which is right. It does not say the hole is the size of the rock (real craters are many times wider than whatever made them), so a learner who takes the picture further is not led into a false belief.

items.bewering: 'n Foto van die Maan wys die kraters duidelik.
items.blok: Die ronde kraters
items.bron: LRO/LROC images (e.g. https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/578) and NASA Moon images show the craters clearly. Minor note, no action needed: a quick phone photo of the full Moon shows mostly the dark patches, and close-up or telescope photos show the craters best.

items.bewering: Daar is geen lug op die Maan nie en ook geen vloeibare water op sy oppervlak nie.
items.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): very thin exosphere, 'not breathable'; 'lack of liquid water'. The word 'vloeibare' correctly sets up the ice exception later in the block.

items.bewering: Sonder lug is daar ook geen wind en geen reën nie.
items.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
items.bron: NASA Space Place (https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/craters/en): without an atmosphere the Moon has 'no wind, no weather'.

items.bewering: Daar is dus geen wind of reën wat die kraters wegvryf nie, en daarom bly hulle baie lank staan.
items.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
items.bron: NASA Space Place (https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/craters/en): on Earth 'weather, water, and plants' wear craters away; the Moon has almost no erosion, so an impact 'becomes frozen in time'. NASA Earth Observatory (https://www.earthobservatory.nasa.gov/IOTD/view.php?id=39769) adds that Earth also has plate tectonics, and that the Moon is worn down only slowly, by later impacts and the solar wind. The cause given is the main one and is true, and 'baie lank' (not 'vir altyd') is the right strength.

items.bewering: Jy sal daar geen see, rivier of plas water kry nie.
items.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): lack of liquid water.

items.bewering: Tog is daar ys diep in party kraters by die Maan se pole.
items.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
items.bron: NASA (https://moon.nasa.gov/news/59/ice-confirmed-at-the-moons-poles/): ice confirmed in 2018 with the Moon Mineralogy Mapper on Chandrayaan-1, mostly in crater shadows near both poles; earlier evidence came from LCROSS (2009). NASA Moon facts: the highest concentrations are 'within darkened craters at the poles'. 'Party' matches the patchy spread reported.

items.bewering: Die Son se lig skyn nooit tot onder in daardie kraters nie.
items.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
items.bron: NASA SVS 'The Moon's Permanently Shadowed Regions' (https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11218) and LRO material (https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/lro-litho5-shadowed.pdf): because the Moon's axis is nearly upright, sunlight never reaches the floors of some craters near the poles, and some have been dark for over two billion years. 'Daardie kraters' points back to 'party kraters', which is correct: not every polar crater is permanently shadowed.

items.bewering: Sonder lug kan 'n mens op die Maan nie asemhaal nie.
items.blok: Hoekom 'n mens 'n ruimtepak nodig het
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): the exosphere 'is not breathable'.

items.bewering: Geen plant en geen dier kan op die Maan se oppervlak leef nie.
items.blok: Hoekom 'n mens 'n ruimtepak nodig het
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): 'cannot support life as we know it'. Edge case checked: dried, dormant tardigrades were spilled when Beresheet crashed in 2019 (Live Science, https://www.livescience.com/66109-tardigrades-moon-israeli-lander.html), but no source says they are alive there, and being dormant is not living. The claim holds.

items.bewering: Ons lyf gebruik die suurstof in die lug wanneer ons asemhaal.
items.blok: Hoekom 'n mens 'n ruimtepak nodig het
items.bron: NHLBI, How the Lungs Work (https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/lungs): oxygen from the air passes into the blood in the air sacs and is carried to the body; this gas exchange is essential to life.

items.bewering: 'n Mens op die Maan moet sy eie suurstof in 'n ruimtepak saamdra.
items.blok: Hoekom 'n mens 'n ruimtepak nodig het
items.bron: NASA ALSJ, Apollo PLSS (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/alsj/WOTM/WOTM-ALMNR-PLSSOPS.pdf): the suit's backpack held an oxygen tank for breathing and ventilation, with a backup oxygen purge system.

items.bewering: Die ruimtepak maak hom heeltemal toe en hou daardie suurstof binne.
items.blok: Hoekom 'n mens 'n ruimtepak nodig het
items.bron: NASA ALSJ PLSS (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/alsj/WOTM/WOTM-ALMNR-PLSSOPS.pdf) and NASA NTRS 19720019467 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720019467/downloads/19720019467.pdf): a sealed suit held at about 3.9 psi with a closed-loop oxygen system.

items.bewering: Die Maan lyk groot in ons lug, maar dit is baie kleiner as die Aarde.
items.blok: Kleiner as die Aarde
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): 'less than a third of the width of Earth'.

items.bewering: Dit is omtrent 'n kwart so breed as ons eie planeet.
items.blok: Kleiner as die Aarde
items.bron: Astronomy.com (https://www.astronomy.com/observing/everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-moon/): diameter about 3,475 km, 'roughly one-fourth' of Earth's width. Earth is about 12,742-12,756 km across (HyperPhysics, https://hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/Solar/sun.html). The ratio is 0.27, so 'omtrent 'n kwart' is right, and it agrees with NASA's 'less than a third'.

items.bewering: Stel jou vier Mane langs mekaar in een lang ry voor. Daardie ry sal omtrent so breed wees as die Aarde self.
items.blok: Kleiner as die Aarde
items.bron: Same figures: 4 x 3,475 km = 13,900 km against Earth's 12,742 km, about 9% wider, so 'omtrent' holds (3.7 Moons span the Earth exactly). Mapping checked: the picture is about width in a row only, and the text says 'breed' and 'ry', so it does not suggest that four Moons would fill the Earth (by volume about 50 would be needed). The image is sound.

items.bewering: Die Maan is dus 'n kleiner bal as die een waarop jy staan.
items.blok: Kleiner as die Aarde
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/).

items.bewering: Die Maan is baie nader aan ons as die Son.
items.blok: Baie nader aan ons as die Son
items.bron: NASA Moon facts (https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/): 384,400 km. HyperPhysics (https://hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/Solar/sun.html): the Sun is on average 149.6 million km away.

items.bewering: Die Son is honderde kere verder van die Aarde af as die Maan.
items.blok: Baie nader aan ons as die Son
items.bron: 149.6 million km / 384,400 km = about 389 (figures as above). NASA My NASA Data (https://mynasadata.larc.nasa.gov/print/pdf/node/847): the Moon is about 400 times closer.

items.bewering: Die Son is ook honderde kere breër as die Maan.
items.blok: Baie nader aan ons as die Son
items.bron: Sun diameter about 1,392,000 km (HyperPhysics, https://hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/Solar/sun.html) / Moon 3,475 km = about 400. NASA APOD (https://apod.nasa.gov/rjn/apod/ap990818.html): 'about 400 times wider than the moon'.

items.bewering: Iets wat verder van jou af is, lyk kleiner as wat dit werklik is.
items.blok: Baie nader aan ons as die Son
items.bron: NASA APOD (https://apod.nasa.gov/rjn/apod/ap990818.html) and Check Your Fact, citing NASA (https://checkyourfact.com/2024/01/22/fact-check-sun-moon-same-size): how big something looks gets smaller with distance, which is why the far bigger Sun looks the same size as the Moon.

items.bewering: Die Son is dus baie groter as die Maan maar ook net soveel kere verder weg. Daarom lyk die twee in ons lug omtrent ewe groot.
items.blok: Baie nader aan ons as die Son
items.bron: NASA APOD (https://apod.nasa.gov/rjn/apod/ap990818.html): about 400 times wider and about 400 times farther, each about half a degree across. NASA My NASA Data (https://mynasadata.larc.nasa.gov/print/pdf/node/847) uses the same reasoning. Mapping checked: the two ratios (about 400 and 389) are only roughly equal, and the block's last sentence says 'omtrent ewe groot', so it does not teach a perfect match. The chain of reasoning is correct.

items.bewering: ruimte: Die baie groot, amper leë plek buite die Aarde se lug.
items.blok: begrip: ruimte
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Outer space' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_space) and New World Encyclopedia (https://www.newworldencyclopedia.org/entry/Outer_space): the region beyond Earth's atmosphere, a near-vacuum holding very sparse particles. 'Amper leë' is exactly right. Read on its own it is true, and it fits the lesson's 'die Maan ... in die ruimte'.

items.bewering: oppervlak: Die hele buitekant van 'n ding.
items.blok: begrip: oppervlak
items.bron: Dictionary.com (https://www.dictionary.com/browse/surface): 'the outer face, outside, or exterior boundary of a thing'. Britannica Dictionary (https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/surface): 'an outside part or layer of something'. Read on its own it is true. In its block it fits 'Die Maan se oppervlak is 'n los laag ...'.

items.bewering: krater: 'n Ronde holte in die grond met 'n rand rondom.
items.blok: begrip: krater
items.bron: OpenStax Astronomy 9.3 (https://openstax.org/books/astronomy/pages/9-3-impact-craters): a roughly circular depression with a raised rim. Read on its own it is true. It covers impact and volcanic craters alike and names no cause, so it does not clash with the block's 'die meeste kraters'.

items.bewering: pool: Op 'n draaiende bal is dit een van die twee punte wat nie in 'n kring rondgaan nie.
items.blok: begrip: pool
items.bron: A pole is where the spin axis meets the surface: those two points turn on the spot while every other point travels in a circle (Weiland's Dutch dictionary, https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/weil004nede12_01/weil004nede12_01_0402.php: 'de aspunten van aarde en hemel'). Using it for the Moon is valid because the Moon does spin, about once every 27 days (NASA Moon facts, https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/). Read on its own it is geometrically exact.

items.bewering: ruimtepak: 'n Pak wat jou eie suurstof saamdra wanneer jy buite in die ruimte of op die Maan is.
items.blok: begrip: ruimtepak
items.bron: NASA ALSJ PLSS (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/alsj/WOTM/WOTM-ALMNR-PLSSOPS.pdf): the suit's backpack carries the breathing oxygen. Read on its own it is true but not complete (a suit also keeps up pressure and controls temperature); nothing in it is false.

opsomming: All 40 claims were checked against sources and every one is confirmed, including the superlatives ('naaste groot buurman', true because of the word 'groot', and the three uses of 'die meeste' / 'byna'-type quantifiers) and the three comparisons (a rock knocking a hole, four Moons in a row, the Sun about 400 times bigger and 400 times farther); nothing is false, nothing is uncertain, and there is no eli10 block.
